subject: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request
messages:
From: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Hi Marissa,

Quick note — we hit an unexpected traffic spike during a marketing campaign this week and exceeded our committed quota for the month. We expected a smaller lift but the models have become core to our checkout flow and token consumption jumped.

We have three asks:
- Can Redwood provision a short-term headroom (48–72 hours) while we stabilize traffic?
- Can the overrun be converted into a one-time true-up rather than hitting our monthly invoice immediately?
- Are there any credits/discounts available for this kind of launch-related overrun?

I attached our usage export for the last 30 days. If you need a PO or additional details for billing, loop in billing@brightlane.ai.

Thanks — we’re trying to avoid customer-facing errors during the weekend.

— Talia
Talia Gomez
Head of Platform, BrightLane
[Attachment: usage_report_Q1.csv (CSV)]

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Talia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the export. I’m sorry you ran into this during launch week. We can absolutely help stabilize traffic short-term. Proposed path:

1) Immediate: open a 72-hour temporary capacity window on your current tier (no model swap) so calls continue to flow while you implement rate smoothing.
2) Billing: instead of immediate invoicing for the overrun, we can convert the excess into a single true-up invoice and offer a one-time 15% credit on the overrun amount if BrightLane agrees to a short, staged commit increase (2-month commitment at a blended rate).
3) Follow-up: Ben (cc’d) will run the numbers and draft a short amendment that we can DocuSign; finance will confirm proration and timing.

If that sounds reasonable, Ben and I will prepare the amendment and the billing team can hold invoicing for the overrun until the true-up is processed. One quick question: do you have an internal PO number or do you need an invoice-first flow?

I’ll kick this to Ben and loop Lauren for approvals on the staged commit margins.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2027 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Hi Talia — attaching a quick sketch of the numbers and the amendment draft (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf). Notes:

- Measured overrun (1/10–1/16): 2.8M tokens over committed quota.
- One-time true-up amount (list): $13,400.
- Offer: convert to true-up and apply 15% one-time credit => $11,390 due.
- Commit path: 2-month bump to 1.5x baseline capacity at a 10% blended discount; this must be executed within 7 days for the credit to apply.
- Invoice timing: we can hold the overrun invoice until amendment is signed and the true-up is billed as a single invoice; if a PO is required, please share number and billing contact.

If BrightLane needs a higher credit to accept a commit, we can consider up to 20% but would need Lauren’s approval for any concession >15% (cc’d).

DocuSign link will be generated once you confirm the PO path — noted in the amendment draft how the proration is calculated.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_amendment_v2.pdf (PDF)]

---
From: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2027 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Thanks Ben — and thanks Marissa. We appreciate the short window and the credit offer. A couple of clarifications from billing:

- BrightLane prefers to receive an invoice-first flow and will issue a PO against the true-up; can Redwood accept PO-based billing for this one-off true-up?
- Can the 15% credit be bumped to 18% if BrightLane executes a 3-month staged commit (instead of 2-month)? We’re willing to take a larger short-term commit to secure better protection for future launches.

We’ll share a PO number by EOD today if acceptable. Also — we’d like interim visibility on metering (token-level breakdown) in the amendment so our finance team can reconcile the single true-up easily.

— Talia

---
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>, BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Ben — we can approve 18% credit conditional on a 3-month staged commit at the proposed blended rate. Finance note: require a signed amendment + PO within 7 business days. Please ensure the amendment includes: token-level metering export schedule (CSV monthly), proration formula, and a clause that the 72-hour emergency window is not billable if the amendment is executed.

Marissa — please confirm with BrightLane on the PO cadence; if they can issue the PO within 48 hours we’ll keep the credit at 18% and lock the hold on invoicing.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Talia Gomez <talia@brightlane.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane Billing <billing@brightlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity redress and invoice hold request

Talia — great news. Lauren has approved the 18% conditional credit for a 3-month staged commit. Quick summary of next steps: 
1) BrightLane to send PO to billing@redwood.com within 48 hours (or let us know timing).
2) We’ll pause invoice generation for the overrun and prepare a single true-up invoice for the adjusted amount ($10,988 after 18% credit).
3) I’ve attached the amendment draft (proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) — Ben will produce a DocuSign envelope when we receive PO.
4) Immediate: 72-hour temporary capacity window is live now; we’ll monitor and follow up if we see persistent elevated QPS.

If you confirm the PO cadence, Ben will spin up the DocuSign and finance will schedule the true-up. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
